answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by requiring every anonymous identity to lock a non-transferable bond, then paying only for work that survives independent replay. A swarm of clones can copy an onyx submission a thousand times, but each clone still locks the same bond, and peers replaying against a shared reference log each copy as a mirror of earlier output and slash it. Forging a thousand votes then costs a thousand bonds plus slashed principal, turning cheap spam into a losing fable no sponsor funds twice.
